newsitem.title: USA: US late spot prods tumble with NYMEX, sellers hide.
newsitem.headline: US late spot prods tumble with NYMEX, sellers hide.

text.p: U.S. spot product prices tumbled late Thursday tracking a futures selloff led by crude oil, with cash traders reporting few deals as sellers balked at parting with barrels at such sharply lower values.

"With the Merc (NYMEX) down so far, sellers just backed away," one Gulf Coast player said, citing exceedingly lethargic activity. "And there's not enough strength in the market to force buyers in," another trader said.
March NYMEX heat settled 1.87 cents a gallon lower, to 61.45 cents, while March gasoline fell 2.24 cents to 65.30 cents.

New York Harbor gasoline differentials were talked a bit lower, with "M5" conventional unleaded offered at 2.0 cents below March futures and "A5" reformulated trading for 0.25 cent over the print, brokers said.
"Things came down maybe a notch, at least notionally," one East Coast gasoline trader said, citing a predominance of talk over action.
Gulf Coast "M4" front-fifth-cycle conventional unleaded was offered at 1.85 cents under the print, slightly weaker, with any-month material pegged at about 2.05 cents under the screen, players said.
